questiontext.text:
Which of the following is NOT a determinant of fertility? Select all that apply:

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

[[ if test="member(1, ta_index)" ]]

Abortion: is the termination of a pregnancy, either naturally (spontaneous abortion or miscarriage) or intentionally (induced abortion). While abortion can affect an existing pregnancy, it does not directly impact the inherent ability to conceive. Therefore, it is not considered a determinant of fertility but rather a decision made regarding an existing pregnancy.

[[/ if ]] [[ if test="member(2, ta_index)" ]]

Amenorrhea: refers to the absence of menstruation, which can occur due to various factors such as hormonal imbalances, stress, excessive exercise, or medical conditions. While amenorrhea can affect fertility by disrupting ovulation (the release of an egg from the ovary), it is a symptom or condition rather than a determinant of fertility itself.

[[/ if ]] [[ if test="member(3, ta_index)" ]]

Sexuality: encompasses various aspects of human sexuality, including sexual orientation, behaviors, desires, and preferences. While sexual behavior may influence the frequency of intercourse and thus impact the chances of conception, sexuality itself is not a direct determinant of fertility. Fertility is primarily determined by biological factors such as reproductive health, hormone levels, and gamete quality, rather than sexual orientation or behavior.

[[/ if ]]
